primary_source.what_it_is_our_words: The author's own copy of his 2008 ACM Interactions column, on his site. It carries TWO rights statements: an ACM permission paragraph inside the article (author's version, personal use, non-commercial redistribution with the paragraph included) and a site-wide footer licence (CC BY-NC 4.0). Both are non-commercial.

licence.read_from: the article's own permission paragraph + the site footer sentence + the CC BY-NC 4.0 legal code

licence.second_quote_le_15_words: not primarily intended for or directed towards commercial advantage or monetary compensation
licence.second_quote_locus: CC BY-NC 4.0 legal code, Section 1(i), the definition of NonCommercial

licence.grants_our_words: Non-commercial copying and adaptation with attribution (site licence); non-commercial redistribution of the author's version with its paragraph (ACM permission).
licence.forbids_our_words: Any use primarily directed at commercial advantage — which a bank's design-generation asset is. The ACM paragraph is narrower still: 'personal use'.

permits_us: names-only — the concept NAMES (signifier, affordance, feedback, mapping, constraint) and the FACT of the 2008 revision, with a pointer to the essay and the ACM citation (Interactions 15(6), 2008); no essay text in node text
why_our_words: Same shape as Laws of UX, which R1 already put in pointer-only for its NC clause: a non-commercial licence is a licence Apollo cannot use. The concepts are Norman's vocabulary and the field's; a node can name them and point. The essay's sentences cannot travel into a commercial deliverable under either notice.
cheap_route_to_lift: jnd.org lists a contact page (consulting-and-talks); ACM permissions for the Interactions column would be a second ask. Price: two messages; the ACM one is a paid republication request in the usual case.
unproven: The Design of Everyday Things (Basic Books) — the book that carries feedback/mapping/constraint at length — was not fetched; its terms are a publisher's. R1 lists it under 'books, not fetchable pages'. Price: n/a — treat as pointer.

Why R1's fetch saw no licence: the footer sentence is plain text; either the 2026 page differs from the 2026-09-02 #236 fetch (unlikely, same day) or the tag-stripping filter dropped the footer block. Not re-run with R1's method. Price: one curl in the sandbox (~0.5K) — not worth it; the licence is now evidenced.

pitfalls.what: The word 'signifier' is doing double duty in Apollo's own vocabulary risk (R1 finding 1 flagged 'gestalt'); 'affordance' is used loosely across the repo's prose. Importing Norman's names without the s202-class collision check invites false retrievals.
pitfalls.owner: conductor — the 'gestalt' collision check should include 'affordance'/'signifier' (grep cost ~0.3K)

pitfalls.what: Two notices with different scopes on one page: a generator that reads the footer (CC BY-NC) and misses the in-article ACM paragraph will redistribute the author's version without the paragraph, breaching the narrower notice even in a non-commercial context.
pitfalls.owner: generator's licence field — store BOTH notice strings for this family
